newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cemex builds solid Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cemex builds solid Q2 results.

text.p: Cemex SA's earnings, cash flow and sales volume were solid in the second quarter even though the Mexican cement supplier's domestic prices softened, analysts said.
Cemex turned in second-quarter earnings of 0.98 pesos per CPO share, topping an average forecast of 0.88 pesos in a Reuters survey of seven industry analysts.

"We liked the report. Cemex had record operating cash flow of $303 million during the quarter, very close to our estimate of $306 million," said Alvaro Shiraishi, an analyst at UBS Securities in New York.
As with most Mexican companies during the quarter, Cemex's bottom line was hurt by lower monetary gains on the income statement, a non-cash item that revalues a company's debt according to inflation.

A bright spot for Cemex was sales volume, which increased along with operating margins in most of its main geographic markets: Mexico, Spain, Venezuela and the United States. The notable exception was Colombia.

The only dark clouds looming over Cemex are cement prices in Mexico, which is only slowly emerging from a long recession, analysts said. Cemex's average realized price during the quarter was $73.50 per tonne, compared with $78 the previous quarter.
Some analysts said it appeared Cemex and its main rival Apasco SA were locked in a price war.

"Neither seems publicly willing to acknowledge that they have been engaged in a mutually destructive price war for more than six months," said Ben Uglow, a cement analyst at Robert Flemings in New York.

Despite the company's Mexico price woes, analysts were impressed with Cemex's financial position. Cemex lowered its interest paid expense by 16 percent during the quarter despite an overall eight percent increase in net debt.

"Financially, this has been Cemex's best quarter since the 1994 devaluation and operationally it was also strong, aside from the eight percent quarter-over-quarter drop in Mexican cement prices," Uglow told Reuters.
Shiraishi said he was most impressed with Cemex's cash flow and forecast that the company would easily meet its objective of reaching $1.2 billion in cash flow for the year.
"The company's solid cash flow is evidence that its geographical diversification strategy is working and should contribute to keeping growth going in the coming quarters," he said.

Shiraishi said Cemex shares were trading at attractive prices. Uglow said that while the shares were not cheap, an improved capital structure and confidence that Mexican demand was rebounding could give the stock more upside.
